official.deadline_note: Applications may be submitted at any time but must be registered in the EMBO portal by 23:59 CEST on 30 October each year; only fully completed applications are considered and selection takes place once a year.
official.application_cycle: Annual round; applications registered by 30 October
official.status_note: The scheme page carries an 'Apply by 30 October' notice, and the application page confirms that selection takes place once a year with outcomes notified by email by mid-November.
benefits: A daily stipend based on the cost of living in the country of the placement or placements.
Cover for living expenses and travel costs connected with the placement.
For journalists, travel and accommodation for a two-day workshop at EMBO in Heidelberg, Germany.
Successful applicants organise their own placements and receive a conditional offer subject to final confirmation from the host institution or newsroom.
eligibility: Applicants must reside in an EMBC Member State, and the placement or placements must also occur in an EMBC Member State.
Placements must be in person; virtual placements are not eligible.
If fellows undertake two or more placements, at least one must be in a different EMBC Member State than the others.
Applicants are not subject to any age restriction.
Journalists must demonstrate relevant experience of working as an employed or freelance journalist as their main occupation, and provide samples of their published or broadcast work.

Life scientists seeking to transition to full-time journalism must hold a master's degree or higher, preferably in a life sciences discipline, and demonstrate a genuine intention to move into journalism as a profession.
requirements: Proposal in English of a maximum of three pages.
Curriculum vitae in English with permanent residential address, email and mobile phone number.
Samples of previous journalism work, which may be in any language.
Prior discussion of the proposal with the proposed host, although formal written acceptance is not required at application stage.
Fellows are expected not to undertake other work during the fellowship and must not report on their host research institution during the fellowship term.
documents: Proposal in English, maximum three pages.
CV in English including permanent residential address, email and mobile contact.
Samples of previous journalism work in any language.
Journalists only: statement that the sabbatical is focused on learning and that they will not report from the host institution.
Researchers only: written confirmation that the proposed placement is a full-time internship in a mainstream media newsroom.
selection_criteria: Genuine desire to broaden and deepen knowledge of science, or a genuine intention to move into journalism as a profession.
Quality of the proposal and the learning outcomes set.
Applicants are judged by the EMBO advisory board, and selection takes place once a year with outcomes notified by email by mid-November.
coverage: Daily stipend based on the cost of living in the country of the placement, published in the EMBO subsistence rates table as 68.00 to 140.00 EUR per day depending on country (for example 93.00 Germany, France, Belgium and the Netherlands; 110.00 Denmark, Iceland, Norway and Switzerland; 100.00 Ireland and the United Kingdom; 68.00 Chile, Croatia, the Czech Republic, Estonia, India, Lithuania, Montenegro, Poland, the Slovak Republic, Slovenia and Taiwan).
Travel allowance published in the same table, from 350 EUR for most European countries to 800 EUR for Chile, India, Singapore and Taiwan, 600 EUR for India and 500 EUR for Israel.
Living expenses and travel costs connected with the placement.
Fellows are responsible for their own social security contributions, taxes or other costs incurred.
application_method: Apply online through the EMBO application portal only; only fully completed applications are considered.
Ensure the application is registered in the portal by 23:59 CEST on 30 October.
On a conditional offer, organise your own placement and obtain final confirmation from the host institution or newsroom.
official.application_route: Online application through the EMBO application portal only, registered by 23:59 CEST on 30 October.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must reside in an EMBC Member State; there is no age restriction and no nationality rule is published.
official.international_eligibility: Both the applicant's residence and the placement must be in an EMBC Member State, so the scheme cannot be used from outside Europe or for a placement outside Europe.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The scheme supports science journalism: journalists seeking placements at research institutions, and life scientists seeking placements in mainstream media newsrooms. Personal blog posts, social media postings, or commentary and review articles in academic journals are not accepted as evidence of prior journalism.
official.research_requirement: For journalists, nomination of the research institution and specific learning and knowledge outcomes. For researchers, nomination of the newsroom and confirmation that the placement will be a full-time internship producing published or broadcast science journalism.
official.duration: Journalists: minimum three months, maximum six months. Researchers transitioning to journalism: minimum three months, maximum twelve months.
official.description: The Maria Leptin | EMBO Science Journalism Fellowships support science journalism by providing journalists with funded placements at research institutions to deepen and broaden their knowledge of the life and associated sciences, and researchers wishing to transition full time into journalism with funded placements in media newsrooms. The scheme was made possible by a private donation from Professor Maria Leptin.
official.english_requirement: The proposal and curriculum vitae must be in English; samples of journalism work may be in any language.

not_confirmed: funding_amount as a single value - EMBO publishes a daily subsistence rate by country, from 68.00 to 140.00 EUR per day, plus a travel allowance of 350 to 800 EUR, so no single award figure exists
funding_period - the stipend is a daily rate multiplied by the length of the placement rather than a published monthly or annual cadence
tuition_coverage - EMBO publishes no tuition statement for this scheme
verification.notes: EMBO's scheme, benefits and eligibility pages plus the official subsistence rates and travel allowance table on embo.org were read in full. The daily rate range and travel allowance figures, the 30 October registration deadline, the mid-November notification, the three-to-six and three-to-twelve month duration bands and the two-day Heidelberg workshop for journalists were all confirmed on the awarding body's domain.

applicant_utility.summary: Both you and your placement must sit inside an EMBC Member State, so this is a European scheme in both directions and cannot be used for a newsroom or lab outside Europe. The money is a daily subsistence rate scaled to the country you are going to - roughly 68 EUR a day in Prague or Warsaw against 140 in Switzerland - plus a travel allowance, so the same fellowship is worth more than twice as much depending on destination. Applications can be filed at any point but must be fully registered in the portal by 23:59 CEST on 30 October, and the fellowship cannot be extended, so get the length right the first time.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Working science journalists based in EMBC Member States who want an in-person research sabbatical, and mid-career life scientists with a master's or doctorate who have already begun reporting and want to move into full-time science journalism.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you live in an EMBC Member State and that your proposed host does too, and talk to the host before you apply - formal written acceptance is not needed yet but prior discussion is.
Pick your length deliberately: three to six months as a journalist, three to twelve as a researcher, with no extension possible.
Write the three-page proposal around concrete learning and knowledge outcomes rather than story ideas you hope to publish.
Assemble three to five published or broadcast samples; blog posts, social posts and academic commentary pieces do not count.
For a researcher-to-journalism switch, secure written confirmation that the placement is a full-time internship in a mainstream media newsroom.
Register the completed application in the EMBO portal well before 23:59 CEST on 30 October.
common_rejection_risks: A placement that is fully virtual rather than in person.
Two or more placements all in the same EMBC Member State, when at least one must be in a different one.
Evidence of journalism consisting of personal blog posts, social media postings, or commentary and review articles in academic journals.
A researcher applicant who cannot show prior reporting on the life sciences or a genuine intention to enter journalism as a profession.
An incomplete application - only fully completed applications are considered.
A proposal that reads as a route to immediate publication opportunities rather than as a sabbatical for learning.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The stipend is a daily subsistence rate scaled to the host country plus a travel allowance. Fellows are responsible for their own social security contributions, taxes and any other costs incurred, and there is no tuition or course-fee element.
document_audit: The CV must be in English and must carry a permanent residential address, email and mobile number - a standard academic CV will not do.
Journalist applicants need an explicit statement that the sabbatical is focused on individual learning and that they will not report from the host institution.
Researcher applicants need a separate written confirmation that the placement is a full-time internship in a mainstream media newsroom.
Journalists are additionally expected to attend a two-day workshop at EMBO in Heidelberg, for which travel and accommodation are provided - diarise it.
alerts: Only one selection round a year: registration closes 30 October at 23:59 CEST and outcomes arrive by email by mid-November.
The fellowship cannot be extended, so plan the length of your sabbatical inside the three-to-six or three-to-twelve month bands.
Fellows must not undertake other work during the fellowship and must not report on their host research institution during the term.
The scheme was made possible by a private donation from Professor Maria Leptin, which is worth knowing if you look for prior awardee profiles.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You file a complete application through the EMBO portal, it must be registered by 23:59 CEST on 30 October, the EMBO advisory board judges the motivation, proposal quality and learning outcomes, and successful applicants are notified by email by mid-November before organising their own placement on a conditional offer.
